A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Re-FORC, with matching authors, forecasting architecture, and inference applications. The main text, equations, figures, references, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Qwen3 forecasting, early-stopping, model-selection, test-time-scaling, and token-allocation experiments, including per-dataset appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original Re-FORC experiments and reports revised results and additional DeepConf comparisons in the main text and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The stated inference procedure changes substantially. v1 Equations (9)–(11) select models or continuations by maximum expected net improvement; v2 Equations (4)–(5) and (12)–(13) rank them by a Gittins index using a cost-to-success-ratio horizon. These rankings are not generally equivalent. v2 also explicitly runs ordinary Re-FORC-scaling traces to completion, whereas v1 Section 4.4 samples them using its early-stopping rule. The forecasting architecture and loss remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Coverage narrows within mathematical reasoning: Minerva disappears from the evaluation suite and appendices. Appendix test-time scaling also loses MATH500, retaining AMC 2024 and AIME 2024/2025; MATH500 remains in other experiments. DeepScaleR training and the three inference applications are retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated confidence-based adaptive comparisons: DeepConf for early stopping and its Online, Tail, and Bottom-10% variants for test-time scaling (Figures 2 and 4; Appendices B.2 and B.5). v1 cites the underlying work but does not evaluate these comparators. Existing S1, voting, forecast-selection, individual-model, and oracle baselines remain.

E3.justification: The added DeepConf comparisons introduce threshold sweeps over 512-token confidence windows, a 2,048-token tail setting, and online sampling with 30% warmup, a median confidence threshold, and 80% vote-based termination. These are additional testing protocols within existing applications. Newly specified limits and sample counts for retained experiments do not establish that those experiments changed or were rerun.

E4.justification: The existing difficulty-versus-token-allocation analysis is narrowed and updated: Minerva's model-size and cost-sensitivity panels in v1 Figure 6 disappear from v2 Figure 15, and the pooled Figure 5 analysis changes accordingly. No new component ablation or separate robustness suite is introduced.

E5.justification: v2 first specifies that test-time-scaling points average over up to 100 randomly sampled size-k subsets per problem. It also qualifies v1's unqualified Monte Carlo N=8 statement with N=4 for Qwen3-1.7B on AIME 2025. These refine statistical-estimation reporting without establishing an increase in repeated runs; no significance testing is added.

E6.justification: Aggregate and retained per-dataset results change substantially, alongside removed Minerva results and added DeepConf curves. For example, the initial Qwen3-1.7B AIME 2025 forecasting correlation changes from 0.40 in v1 Figure 8 to 0.38 in v2 Figure 7. v2 Figure 4 reports peak-compute advantages over the strongest DeepConf variant of 13.9, 8.4, and 7.5 percentage points for 1.7B, 4B, and 8B. Changed policies and aggregation pools prevent interpreting all version-to-version shifts as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: v2 adds the binary-reward closed form g=1−λt/p, explicitly defines the horizon minimizing λt/ψ(t), and adds Appendix A with four propositions and proofs covering the index, horizon selection, binary expected improvement, and stopping-rule equivalence. v1 has the implicit index equation and stopping inequalities but lacks these formal definitions and proofs.

C1.justification: The headline efficacy claims are substantially narrowed or redefined. Model selection changes from 4% higher accuracy at equal compute and 55% compute savings to 1.7 percentage points higher peak accuracy and up to 12% savings. Test-time scaling changes from 7%/11% low/high-compute improvements to an average 9.9-point peak-compute advantage over confidence baselines. The introduction also drops the 'first method' claim, while retaining the same three principal applications.

C2.justification: Two substantive interpretations change. v1 presents Pandora's trajectory switching as beneficial at low compute; v2 explains its overhead below 25k tokens and locates its benefits at larger budgets. v1 interprets high cost sensitivity as concentrating larger models' effort on the hardest problems; v2 Figure 5 and Section 6 instead describe reduced allocation to the hardest problems across model sizes. Existing data-collection and overconfidence limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies an 8,192-token thinking limit, evaluation sampling of 32 responses per problem except four for MATH500, and cost accounting in 512-token chunks. Appendix B.6 adds DeepConf implementation details: post-hoc top-20 log-probabilities from a separate forward pass with matching templated prompt and response context. These improve documentation without proving changes to previously unspecified settings.

R1.justification: Genuine additions include SCALAR and Manvi et al.'s concurrent forecasting work. v2 emphasizes its realization of Achille and Soatto's framework and explicitly contrasts forecasting with confidence-based methods; DeepConf and e1 were already cited in v1. The broad related-work structure remains, while the lengthy algorithmic-mutual-information discussion is removed. Publication updates and duplicate-reference consolidation are not new research coverage.

P1.justification: Sections 4 and 6 undergo substantial rewriting, with clearer distinctions among inference variants and revised explanations of results. The user-cost example moves from a footnote into the introduction, limitations are compressed and moved after the conclusion, an Impact Statement is added, and the appendix is reorganized into theory followed by experiments.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column to a two-column layout, with extensively resized figures and rewritten captions. Appendix early-stopping and scaling grids are reorganized around datasets with model sizes side by side. Legends gain DeepConf entries, model-selection axes are revised, and forecasting plots are redistributed across pages. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the efficiency claims easier to assess through evaluated adaptive DeepConf baselines, explicit inference derivations, implementation disclosures, and corrected interpretations of Figures 4–5. These benefits outweigh the limited loss of benchmark coverage. The overall gain remains qualified by reporting inconsistencies, including 10% model-selection savings in Figure 3 versus 12% in the abstract and Section 6; changed headline performance is not itself evidence of improvement.
